newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Santos unions, steel firm to continue talks.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Santos unions, steel firm to continue talks.

text.p: Union officials from Brazil's port of Santos said they would hold fresh talks with steel firm Cosipa and they may present a new cost-cutting proposal aimed at solving a labor dispute.
"Cosipa is waiting for us to make a new analysis," said Antonio Pinho, second secretary of the Santos Stevedores' Union, which is heading talks on the part of the unions.
"We may present our third proposal. We will study whether it is necessary for us to call an assembly to discuss this," he said after talks with Compahia Siderurgica Paulista.
Union members last month staged two strikes at Santos in protest at Cosipa's decision to use its own workers to load and unload at its private terminal.

A union official last week said it had presented a plan that would cut costs for Cosipa by 60 percent, virtually removing any further chance of a strike. But the steel firm found aspects of the plan unclear, according to Pinho.
The next meeting between the two sides is scheduled on June 4 at 1400 local/1700 GMT.
